function.name: cmd_controller_execute
function.description: Executes a system-level command using os.system() on Windows operating systems. It can execute single or multiple commands chained with '&&'. Note that the provided function is in Python 3 syntax.

command.description: The system command to be executed. To execute multiple commands, separate them with '&&'. For example, 'dir && echo done'.

unit.description: Specifies the unit of measure for the command if applicable. This is not utilized by os.system() directly but can be used for logging or analysis purposes.

message.reasoning:
The user asks: "is chrome is installed". They want to check if Chrome is installed. We need to use the provided tool to execute a system command. On Windows, we can check if Chrome is installed by checking the existence of its executable path. Typically Chrome is installed at "C:\Program Files (x86)\Google\Chrome\Application\chrome.exe" or "C:\Program Files\Google\Chrome\Application\chrome.exe". We can use the 'where' command: where chrome.exe. Or we can check registry. But simplest: use 'where chrome.exe' and see if it returns a path. So we can run a command: where chrome.exe. That will output the path if found. If not found, error. So we can call the function.

We need to provide JSON with command: "where chrome.exe". The unit can be omitted or set to "N/A". We'll do that.
